highlights: Urban delivery platform combines cameras, LiDAR and GPS with onboard navigation
Manufacturer describes swappable batteries and replaceable tires for fleet operations
Navigation combines mapping and neural networks with human oversight

The product page rates speed at 21 km/h and range at 32 km. Speed is a technical manufacturer rating rather than a legal sidewalk speed; distance range has unspecified route, load and weather conditions and is not battery runtime in hours.

Native animated labels specify 30% maximum grade, turn-in-place, swappable batteries, replaceable tires and packing for four 18-inch pizzas. Grade is not degrees, and packing does not establish kg payload, cargo litres or complete body dimensions.

The February 26, 2026 launch announcement identifies Jetson Orin NX onboard computing and NVIDIA simulation/training tools. The current product page describes human oversight and a Pilot Terminal with ETA, navigation, obstruction alerts and map annotations for intervention; autonomy does not establish unstaffed operation in every environment.

The launch release describes road/bike-lane expansion only where permitted and up to three times longer uptime without a stated baseline. Generic community copy still describes remote pilots; exact historic-generation mapping remains unresolved. Service delivery-time and fee claims are separate from per-charge endurance, legal authorization and robot purchase price.

highlights: Coco Robotics describes a company founded in 2020 and introduced Coco 2 on February 26, 2026. The legacy Coco product route redirects to Coco 2; it does not independently establish a second named historical hardware configuration.

Urban robotic delivery combines onboard perception/mapping, neural-network navigation, human oversight and a Pilot Terminal. Generic community remote-pilot wording lacks exact generation mapping; the current service and technical platform keep their distinct scopes.

Merchant delivery and advertising are services, while Urban Robotics Platform and Pilot Terminal are software/operations tools. Fleet size, order totals, uptime, lower fees, zero-emissions and world-largest claims are manufacturer business/marketing statements, not per-robot endurance, purchase price, independent lifecycle/safety findings or exclusive superiority.

companyFocus.reviewNotes: Batch140. Seven hashed manufacturer HTTP200 responses inspected as native HTML and DOM text nodes; animated single-letter labels reconstructed from actual native text preserving spaces/NBSP, not OCR or image inspection.21/32 headline values verified against Speed(kph)/Range(km) label containers. Coco2 February26, 2026 launch retained. Technical21km/h, 32km distance and30percent grade remain distinct from legal speed, hour runtime, degrees and independent tests. Four 18in pizza packing is not kg payload/volume/body size. Current human oversight and PilotTerminal retained alongside dated launch autonomy and unversioned community remote-pilot copy; no invented Coco1 identity. Legacy/coco redirects to Coco2. Software/services are not additional hardware. Original three highlights, discovery, ID and media preserved. No form, login, message, contact, quote, transaction, media reuse or independent safety/sustainability/exclusive superiority proof. Complete historic portfolio and leadership remain unproven.
